q-0315.answer:
Surah An-Nisaa (4) — The Women · 176 ayahs · Medinan

Main teachings:
• Except those who join and take refuge with a people with whom you have a pact of peace, or people of Dhimmah, then treat them as you treat the people with whom you have peace.
• Their hearts were truthful and their limbs obedient with the righteous acts they were commanded, all the while abandoning the evil they were prohibited from doing.
• If the person who dies in Kalalah has two sisters, they get two-thirds of the inheritance.
• They dwell in Fitnah. As-Suddi said that the Fitnah mentioned here refers to Shirk.
• They will not be able to avoid, avert, evade or elude the Hellfire.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0360.answer:
Surah An-Nahl (16) — The Bee · 128 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• Finding Consolation in the Reminder of Those Who came before
• It will not be delayed for them, rather they will be taken quickly from the place of gathering, with no calling to account.
• Those who oppose you, for Allah has decreed that this should happen.
• They will see and hear better than they have ever seen and heard before.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0427.answer:
Surah As-Sajda (32) — The Prostration · 30 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• They pray the voluntary night prayer and forego sleep and resting on a comfortable bed.
• Their hearts believed in the signs of Allah, and they did as the signs of Allah dictate, i.
• Turn away from these idolators, and convey that which has been revealed to you from your Lord.
• We shall avenge Ourselves on those who do that in the strongest possible terms.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0676.answer:
Surah At-Tin (95) — The Fig · 8 ayahs · Meccan

Main teachings:
• To the Hellfire. This was said by Mujahid, Abu Al-'Aliyah, Al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and others.
• In the recompense that will take place in the Hereafter.
• It would not be correct to exclude the believers from this, because some of them are also overcome by the senility of old age.

Full ayah text and tafsir are available in the sources below.

q-0742.answer: Scholars classify the 114 surahs by where they were first revealed: approximately **86 surahs are Meccan** (revealed before Hijrah in Makkah) and **28 are Medinan** (revealed after Hijrah in Madinah). Meccan surahs often focus on faith, tawhid, and the Hereafter; Medinan surahs often address law, community, and governance. Individual surah pages show each surah's revelation type.

c-0014.answer:
Jihad means struggle or striving — from the root j-h-d, exertion. The Quran uses it for effort far beyond battle: "Strive against them with it [the Quran] — a great jihad" (25:52) describes preaching; striving to serve parents, to give charity, to control one's temper and desires are all jihad in the Prophet's ﷺ usage: "The mujahid is the one who strives against his own soul" (Jami' at-Tirmidhi 1621).

Armed jihad exists — the Quran is not pacifist — but it is regulated war, not holy rage: declared by legitimate authority, only against combatants, with civilians absolutely protected. The Prophet ﷺ forbade killing women and children (Sahih al-Bukhari 3015); Abu Bakr's (r.a.) marching orders to his army codified it: no killing of children, women, the elderly or monks in their monasteries, no destruction of trees or livestock (Muwatta Malik 21.10). Treachery is forbidden even against enemies (Quran 8:58). The word's hijacking — by extremists who violate every one of these rules, and by polemicists who quote the extremists — does not change fourteen centuries of legal definition.
